Arrow schemas

Source: R/handles.R
arrow_schema.Rd

arrow_schema() makes a schema handle from a format string, from an R object, or from any schema, array or stream handle. A handle can come from zuarrow, from 'nanoarrow' or from any producer that uses its layout, such as 'arrow', 'duckdb' or an 'ADBC' driver.

Usage

arrow_schema(x)

Arguments

x

A format string, an R object, or a schema, array or stream handle.

Value

A schema handle of class c("zuarrow_schema", "nanoarrow_schema").

Details

A single string is read as an Arrow format string, such as "i" for int32 or "tsu:UTC" for a microsecond timestamp in UTC. Any other R object gives the schema it would be written with: a data frame gives a struct with one field per column. On a handle, arrow_schema() never raises on the content: it copies the schema, or asks a stream for it.

format() gives the type notation Arrow's own tools print, such as int64 or struct<x: int32>, and print() shows it.

See also

arrow_metadata() for schema metadata, arrow_equal() to compare schemas.

Examples

arrow_schema("l")
#> <zuarrow_schema> int64
arrow_schema(data.frame(x = 1:3, y = c("a", "b", "c")))
#> <zuarrow_schema> struct<x: int32, y: string>
format(arrow_schema(as.Date("2026-10-21")))
#> [1] "date32"
